findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: The method collects groupResource.getId() (the generated authorization-resource UUID) into the returned set, and line 122 passes that same value to hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...). But group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with name = the group id while the resource id is a generated UUID, and hasPermission resolves its argument via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). For a per-group resource the lookup therefore misses and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource, so the set never contains real group ids. Callers use this set as a group-id filter: UsersResource.searchForUser puts it into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute and UsersResource.getUsersCount and BruteForceUsersResource pass it to the user provider. Consequences: (1) per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions never restrict the database query, so pagination is applied to the unfiltered user list and users the caller can see can be missing from a page, and the count is not group-restricted; (2) when the caller has VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the all-groups resource, the set contains the all-groups resource UUID, which no group has, so user search and count return no users at all. The new tests only grant per-group member permissions and use first=-1/max=-1, so neither case is covered.

findings.title: canManage() accepts VIEW scope, so a view-only admin can create groups
findings.body: canManage() (no group argument) returns true when the caller has any of VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource, while canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage(), which uses this method, so an admin granted only VIEW on all groups can create top-level groups. The javadoc added to GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() repeats the VIEW-or-MANAGE rule, so both the implementation and the documentation should be corrected to require MANAGE.

findings.title: All-groups permission is ignored once any per-group resource exists
findings.body: hasPermission only falls back to the all-groups resource when resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) returns null. As soon as a per-group resource exists for any scope, only that resource is evaluated and the all-groups resource is never consulted. Concrete case: an admin holds MANAGE on the all-groups resource and some per-group permission (for example VIEW_MEMBERS) was created for group G; canManage(G), canView(G) and canManageMembership(G) then look only at G's resource, find no MANAGE/VIEW, and deny the action even though the global permission grants it. Global and per-group permissions should be combined (with DENY overriding) instead of treating the existence of a per-group resource as a replacement for the global one.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc names the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says the ForbiddenException is thrown when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but the implementation checks canManageMembers(GroupModel). This documents the wrong permission required to call the method.
